notes: Parses to the standard manifest key set (author, description, homepage, keywords, license, name, repository, version); 2-space indent per project convention. The version key doubles as the minimum tp version session-start.sh compares against - overloaded but deliberate and documented at session-start.sh:6-8. Confirmed the read works by running the hook against a shimmed tp: v0.35.0 passes the gate, v0.34.3 is refused with exit 2.

Valid JSON; SessionStart and PreToolUse carry matchers and Stop correctly carries none. The Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit matcher lines up with the two path keys both PreToolUse hooks extract. The 10-second declared timeout is now backed by my own measurement rather than an estimate: see the stop-role-incomplete.sh row. The fourth script is deliberately absent here - the two role agents register it themselves.

Re-exercised from /private/tmp with TP_ROUND_DIR spelled through the /tmp symlink, the case that regressed in round 4. Allowed (exit 0): the physical spelling of the unit's own .part file, and its relative spelling. Denied (exit 2, stderr naming the one writable file): a sibling role's .part, the final .ndjson name the driver renames to, and the no-environment case - i.e. the allowlist still fails closed when it cannot build itself.

Exercised, not read. Denied with exit 2 and a hint naming the owning tp command: .tp/config.json, .TP/config.json, .tp/locks/../config.json, /a/b/x.tasks.json, .tp-review/r1/x.json, and a backslash-carrying spelling (fails closed with a stated reason). Ran all three arms with shimmed tp binaries. Current tp inside a cycle: exit 0, 631 bytes of tp resume --compact on stdout, stderr empty, and every empty collection in that payload serialises as [] (blockers, bookkeeping, changes, kept). Stale tp: exit 2, stdout empty, message plus install hint on stderr. Outside a cycle: exit 0, both streams empty, session not blocked. Channels are clean and the injected payload is bounded by an existing command's compact form.

Round 5's hook-exceeds-its-declared-timeout does not reproduce; I measured it myself rather than repeating the verdict. BSD awk 20200816, 1MB single line: valid line 0.57s (exit 0), valid-prefix-then-garbage 0.59s (exit 2), invalid at character one 0.06s (exit 2); four concurrent 1MB scans finished in 0.83s wall. Against the declared 10s that is a ~17x margin idle and ~12x under fourfold concurrency, and the numbers match the comment's recorded measurements, so the comment is now an accurate claim rather than the 'bounds the time' one it used to make. Verdicts unchanged and the refusal message names the file and the escalate alternative.

Ran it (go test ./internal/cli -run TestRunLock_ -count=1: ok). Cross-process test, so it exercises the real exit surface rather than a double: the child's tp set lands in <4s while the run lock is held, and the second acquirer's error is asserted by type and by literal lock path. No JSON payload of its own; nothing in this role's domain beyond the hint/path pinning, which is correct.

Round 5's degraded-scan-reports-clean-in-json is repaired; I re-ran the repro rather than reading the fix. Truncated .tp/config.json -> {project_config:true, deviations:[], skipped:['.tp/config.json']}; chmod 000 config -> same; unreadable subdir -> skipped:['sub'] beside real deviations; all three keep skipped under --quiet while the stderr warning goes silent, so the payload a driver branches on carries the fact. deviations is always [] never null; --strict exits 1 only on deviations. Residual, deliberate and now visible: --strict still exits 0 when skipped is non-empty and deviations is 0 - the degradation is signalled in the payload, not the exit code, which is the right call since exit 1 already means 'deviation found'.

This file changed under me mid-round (commit 04b0c89 made RunLockHeld return (bool, error)); I re-derived on the post-change build. Ran it: a second driver over a live run exits 4 with {error,code,hint} on stderr, hint naming the cycle, refusal prompt not a backoff. All three run_state arms observed against a real in-flight run: in_flight while held, crashed with the lock file present and unheld, and - the new arm - in_flight plus an output.Notice warning when .tp/locks is chmod 000, silenced by --quiet. The enum stays the documented three values; an unprobeable probe did not invent a fourth. No slice reaches JSON here.

Ran it (go test ./internal/engine -run 'RunLock|WithRunLock' -count=1: ok). The one assertion in this role's domain - that the gitignore advisory is an output.Notice and so honours --quiet - is written the right way round at L167-190: the loud half induces the failure by making .tp/.gitignore a directory before the quiet half asserts silence, so the quiet assertion cannot pass against a branch that never ran. Hint text and lock path pinned at L92-94. No JSON-shape surface of its own.

Data manifest, no executable surface. Parsed with python3 json.load: valid. version 0.35.0 is what session-start.sh reads as its minimum; confirmed by running that hook, which correctly refuses the lagging PATH tp v0.34.2. Nothing in this role's domain.

Valid JSON (python3 json.load). All three commands resolve under ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/ and each target exists at mode 0755 (ls -l hooks/), so none fails open on a lost executable bit. Denied (rc=2): .tp/config.json, .tp/./config.json, .tp//config.json, .tp/locks/../config.json, .TP/config.json, /x/.tp/local.json, *.tasks.json, .tp-review/ contents, notebook_path, both backslash and \u0074 escapes. Ran six branches. Lagging tp v0.34.2 -> exit 2 naming the minimum; CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT unset -> self-locates and still judges (rc=2); tp off PATH -> named refusal + install hint; a v9.9.9 shim -> rc=0; a shim printing no version -> refused; missing manifest -> refused. Every failure path is reported, none swallowed; version_part coerces a non-numeric component to 0 so the arithmetic test cannot error.

Round-5 hook-timeout-bound-unmet is not reproducible on this machine; the repaired comment's numbers are accurate. Measured here (BSD awk 20200816, load avg 6.1): 1MB single valid line 0.61s rc=0; 1MB valid-then-tail-garbage 0.66s rc=2; invalid at char one 0.06s rc=2; four concurrent 1MB scans 0.89s wall. Against the declared 10s that is ~15x margin. Escalation checked first and alone; fails closed when the env names no findings file.

Cross-process test 9. WriteFile 0o600, filepath.Join throughout, EvalSymlinks before comparing lock paths. Driver goroutine synchronised by acquired/release/held channels with a deferred close+join; no unpaired lock. Ran: go test -race -run RunLock ./internal/cli/... - passes race-clean in 5.3s.

Round-5 stat-error-conflated-with-absent is repaired, verified by running. Ran tp validate --project on four configs: readable -> project_config:true; chmod 000 file -> true + skipped; unparseable -> true + skipped; .tp dir chmod 000 (real os.Stat EACCES) -> project_config:false WITH skipped:[.tp/config.json] plus 'warning: project config unreadable ... permission denied' on stderr; absent -> false, no skipped. fileExists discriminates fs.ErrNotExist.

RunLockHeld drops both os.Stat's and TryLock's error into 'not held'. Its doc argues only the ENOENT case; EACCES/EIO are a different question. Spec test 35 makes this probe the discriminator between in_flight and crashed, so an unreadable .tp/locks reports a LIVE run as crashed. Same class as the validate_project.go row repaired this round. Ran the mechanism (stat inside a chmod-000 dir gives 'permission denied'); the end-to-end misreport needs a second uid. WithRunLock itself is clean.

WriteFile 0o600, MkdirAll 0o755 for dirs, filepath.Join everywhere. holdRunLock observes a real second acquirer rather than asserting the refusal from one take; the gitignore-notice test induces the failure and asserts the loud half before the --quiet half, so the quiet assertion is not a tautology. Ran: go test -race -run RunLock ./internal/engine/... - race-clean.

Static manifest, 2-space indent per the project convention, no trailing comma, valid JSON. version 0.35.0 is the release under audit and is the value session-start.sh:86 parses as its minimum, so the two do not drift. Nothing else in this role's domain appears in it.

2-space indent, a description that names all three registrations, every ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} command resolving to a file that exists and is mode 0755. Independently re-checked the one apparent orphan: pre-tool-use-role-write-allow.sh is absent here by design and registered instead at agents/tp-reviewer.md:9 and agents/tp-auditor.md:9, pinned by internal/cli/plugin_agents_test.go:30 - so no dead script.

set -u, every helper documented with the rule it enforces and the reason it fails closed on an absent environment. Mode 0755 confirmed by ls, so the hook cannot silently fail open - the class CLAUDE.md names. Considered and rejected: the path extraction (104-106) and env-derived name (42-47) recur in the sibling hooks, but each is a standalone POSIX script the runtime invokes alone, and a rename reddens role_write_symlink_test.go and hooks_stop_test.go.

set -u, mode 0755. normalize() and denied() each carry the rule and the concrete spelling that motivated them (.tp/./config.json, .TP/config.json on APFS); the backslash refusal at 102-111 records the trade it takes rather than asserting it is safe. No TODO/FIXME anywhere under hooks/ (searched). Awk is inlined rather than shelled out to python/jq, keeping the file dependency-free like its siblings.

set -u, mode 0755, one fail() sink so the install hint is written once. version_number/version_part/version_below are three small named functions rather than one inline comparison, each documented; the comment at 41-49 explicitly corrects an earlier draft that claimed the opposite, which is the honest form. No TODO. The CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT fallback (33-38) keeps the manifest path derivable without the variable.

Longest file of the ten, but the length is the inline awk JSON grammar, split into eight small named functions mirroring the JSON productions. set -u, mode 0755. The round-5 comment addition (65-78) records a measured residual risk and the trade not taken rather than deleting the concern. No TODO; nothing dead - ch(), the block path and charsplit are all reachable. Reason strings at 282-288 differ per branch, so a refusal names which condition failed.

One 53-line cross-process test with a doc comment naming what it pins and the deadlock it rules out. Goroutine handshake uses three named channels and a deferred close+join, so no leaked goroutine; TempDir is EvalSymlinks-resolved. No bare var slice, no TODO. go test -race ./internal/cli passes (42.9s); golangci-lint run reports 0 issues, so the unused/unparam/dupl gate is clean on this file.

Re-derived over the round-5 change. All four JSON-bound slices are make([]T,0) (24,130,131) or []any{} literals (118,124) - the null-vs-[] rule holds on both new early-return branches too. runValidateProject is 75 lines (99-173), under the 80 bound; every unexported helper carries a doc comment. fileExists(bool,error) is used by both callers and neither drops the error: 108-121 returns early, config_extract.go:273 fails closed on it. No TODO, no %w propagation site.

Both propagated errors wrap with %w (101,116); the one swallowed failure is deliberately non-fatal and routed through output.Notice (110) with the regression it prevents recorded. Exported RunLockBusyError, RunLockPath, RunLockHeld, WithRunLock and Hint all have doc comments; Error() is the idiomatic stdlib-interface exception and the type's own comment carries it. Longest func is 31 lines. deadcode (scripts/check-deadcode.sh, exit 0) reports nothing here, so no exported symbol is orphaned.

Six tests, each with a doc comment stating the rule rather than restating the code. Helpers runLockTarget/holdRunLock are the shared setup that keeps the tests from duplicating it, and holdRunLock's release is idempotent so the defer + explicit call at 99 cannot double-close. Cleanup restores output.Configure (168). No bare var slice, no TODO; -race clean.
readCycle goes through the same oracle path tp resume uses; tp run --dry-run printed the identical next_units/phase/round object tp resume prints.
Releasability is checked before caps and returns StopConverged; TestRunDriver_StopsConvergedWhenTheOracleReportsRelease and TestRunExitCodes_ConvergedExitsZero pin exit 0. Suite green.

StopNoUnits exists and is last in precedence; TestRunDriver_EmptyNextUnitsStopsWithNoUnits and TestRunExitCodes_NoUnitsExitsFour cover it. Live, next_units was never empty on a non-releasable cycle I could construct.
Ran it: three review-role children spawned in one iteration (seq 1,2,3 with overlapping timestamps in run-spec.json), while review-record and implement each ran alone.

succeeded() reads exit code plus the on-disk durable write only. Proved by mutation of the input: a fake exiting 0 but writing nothing was retried and stopped the run unit-failure; a fake writing the role file succeeded.
capStop is consulted between iterations. Live: with run_max_units=2 the first iteration's three units all ran, then the run stopped cap-units - the documented one-iteration overshoot.
No memory or retrieval layer: no embedding/vector/DB dependency in go.mod and no such code in internal/ (searched). tp resume is the handoff and I drove it across a driver restart.
No self-clear: the driver spawns a fresh child per unit via exec.Command and never signals or resets a caller's context. Confirmed by the per-attempt env dumps, each a new process.
No scheduler: tp run has no interval/cron/daemon flag, and no cron or scheduler code exists in internal/ (searched). It runs until it stops - observed on five separate runs.
No convergence policy change: the oracle reads the same recorded rounds and clean-round counts v0.33.0 owns; the driver adds only unit selection. tp run never records a round itself.

No parallel writing units: concurrentBatch truncates to one as soon as a non-concurrent kind appears, enforced in the driver as well as the oracle. Observed live - record and implement units always ran alone.
No prose parsing: spawn records only the exit code and duration; the sole content read is spend_key from the log's final line. My fakes printed arbitrary prose and none of it influenced any outcome.
No new decomposition or review semantics: the eight kinds map onto the existing phases and their brief commands are the existing tp subcommands (tp next --brief, tp review, tp audit, tp resume).

TP_RUNNER_SEAM resolves to a runner with the four positional args and spend_key total_cost_usd, read from the driver's own env and outranking every layer. I used it for every live run in this audit and it overrode a configured runner each time; the internal/fakerunner package records argv, env, spawn and exit times.

Ran a runner with args ['{nope}']: exit 2, 'runner.args[0]: "{nope}" is not a placeholder tp resolves', and no child was spawned (no run directory entries, no fake invocation records). ResolveUnitRunner is pure and returns argv, so the failure is structurally before exec.

Ran both directions: a fake writing total_cost_usd=0.25 as the last log line gave every unit spend_usd 0.25 and totals 1.25; the same fake printing to stdout while the template owned the log gave spend null. A runner with no spend_key reported the unmetered notice.

Observed the null-then-updated pair directly: the driver-error run left all three rows with exit_code null and duration null (the children never ran), while completed runs carry exit_code, duration_seconds and log_path on every row.
Ran tp run --dry-run on a fresh project: it listed the three review-role units with kind/id/brief_command plus phase and round, exited 0, wrote no .tp/run-spec.json and left no run directory.

Ran --status against an in-flight run (run_state in_flight, stop_reason null, units_done 3), a stopped run (full report with caps, last_unit, spend, stop_reason) and no run state (exit 3 with a hint). TestRunStatus_CarriesTheDivergenceSignalsOnAnAuditPhaseStop covers the audit-phase signals.
Read the .tp/.gitignore a fresh tp init writes: it carries local.json, locks/ and the four new entries run-*.json, runs/, rounds/ and last_failure-*.json.

Ran all seventeen boundary cases through tp set --workflow. Every numeric field accepted both documented endpoints and rejected exactly one step outside: units 1/10000 vs 0/10001, seconds 60/604800 vs 59/604801, budget 0/10000 vs 10001, unit budget 0/1000 vs 1001, retries 0/5 vs 6.

Ran it: the six attempts of three retried units took seq 1-6 and six distinct log paths. clearUnitArtifacts removes both the final findings name and any stale .part immediately before each spawn, so a leftover cannot answer for the retry.

Every DurableWrite branch is a state read of the named artifact with no baseline - no 'before' is captured anywhere in the driver. An unreadable artifact answers false rather than erroring, which is why the Stop hook and the driver can decide the same condition.

Ran all four under TP_UNATTENDED=1 (each exit 2 with its own hint) and each without it (exit 0). Also ran the cap cases: equal and lower accepted, and a budget field set to 0 while a non-zero resolves refused.

Drove the loop live through review (role -> record) and into implement and audit phases in two scratch projects. TestRunDriver_AdvancesThroughImplementAndStopsConverged pins the converged terminus; suite green.

The informative experiment: configured runner.env with TP_UNATTENDED=0 and dumped the child's env. The child saw TP_UNATTENDED=1. The same run showed a forged TP_RUN_ID overwritten with the real ULID and MYVAR passing through untouched.
Ran a fake that escalates: stop_reason escalation, all three records preserved on disk, each unit row at attempt 1 (no retry charged), and .tp/last_failure-spec.json absent afterwards.

Ran it: three concurrent siblings each wrote $TP_RUN_DIR/$TP_UNIT_SEQ-escalation.json (1-, 2-, 3-) with the exact §5.2 field set and their own unit_id; tp escalate exits 2. Outside a run it is exit 2 usage: 'TP_RUN_DIR is not set'.

Ran a fake exiting 9: .tp/last_failure-spec.json holds unit_kind, unit_id, phase, exit_code 9, a tp-authored summary naming the command and log, and at. tp resume and tp brief both surfaced it verbatim in a later process.

Ran `claude plugin validate .` and `claude plugin validate --strict .` from the repo root - both passed, exit 0. plugin.json declares name tp, version 0.35.0 (the SessionStart preflight's minimum) and ships no binary.

Ran six crafted payloads covering all four denied path classes across Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit (all exit 2) plus a source path and a Bash payload (both exit 0). hooks.json's matcher is exactly Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit.
Ran it: a role unit with an escalation record present was allowed even with an unparseable .part; the same unit without the record was blocked; a non-role kind never fired.

Ran tp review spec.md twice in the same project: without TP_ROUND_DIR the prompt says 'Write this round's findings to: review-r1-implementer.ndjson'; with TP_ROUND_DIR=/tmp/tp-r6/rd it says '/tmp/tp-r6/rd/role-implementer.ndjson.part'.

Ran a three-row merge where two roles reported §1.1 under different classes and a third reported §2.0 alone: location_clusters carried exactly one entry {location §1.1, roles [implementer,tester], severities [major,minor], count 2}, and merged_count stayed 3.
MechanizePhaseQualifier is appended to the mechanize branch, and skills/tp/SKILL.md carries the identical sentence twice (grep -c = 2), pinned by TestDocsCarryTheMechanizePhaseQualifier.

Each cap has its own counter and reason (TestCapStop_EachCapIsProducedByItsOwnCounter); TestRunDriver_ACapStopConcludesNothing asserts no round recorded, no phase converged, no task closed. Live, my cap-units stop left .tp-review untouched.

file_summary carries Truncated bool and TotalChanged int as payload fields (not notices), with total_files still the audited count and truncated derived from the two counts rather than from which branch ran - so --quiet cannot erase it.

Ran it: tp show with 0 and with 2 args -> exit 2, and the 0-arg hint is 'usage: tp show <id>', naming the missing argument. cobra's own built-in `tp completion bash extra` -> exit 2. A command with a nil Args validator (tp status) is deliberately untouched, since cobra substitutes ArbitraryArgs and no violation can arise.
Ran it: the merge summary carries inputs [{path, parsed 1, skipped 1}]. A file whose only content line was malformed exited 1 naming that input; a file with one good and one bad line exited 0.

Observed the same number three ways in one run: three units retried once gave totals.units 6, six unit rows, and --status units_done 6. A run stopped by run_max_units=2 counted 3 attempts against the cap.

highestPrecedence takes every satisfied condition at once rather than testing in order, so the ordering has one home. Observed live: run_max_units=2 with failing units recorded unit-failure (rank 3), not cap-units (rank 7), exactly as the order predicts.

Ran all three states: --status during an in-flight run reported in_flight; after a normal stop, stopped; after I cleared stop_reason to simulate a driver death, crashed. --status itself took no lock (it ran while the driver held one).

Ran two separate runs over one cycle. Run 1 left three role files in .tp/rounds/spec/review-r1/; run 2 (a new run id) omitted all three roles and spawned only the review-record unit. The round dir is keyed by cycle, not by run.

Dumped the real child environment: TP_RUN_ID=01M1AH8Y... (26-char ULID), TP_RUN_DIR absolute, TP_ROUND_DIR=<root>/.tp/rounds/spec/review-r1, TP_ROUND=1, TP_FILE=spec.tasks.json, TP_UNIT_ID, TP_UNIT_KIND, TP_UNIT_SEQ, TP_PHASE, TP_UNATTENDED=1, cwd the repo root.

Re-checked against the sharpened spec (8d6e6a7). Ran tp resume: next_units[0] is {review-role, implementer, 'tp review spec.md'} with round 1; next_action.payload.unit is {review-role, implementer}, while command/brief_command/summary keep phase-level forms. soloIfNotConcurrent truncates to one for a non-concurrent kind. Spec-side observation only: §4.1 line 352 still lists brief_command among the halves rendering next_units[0], which test 38 now exempts.
Ran the same incomplete role unit twice: with stop_hook_active false it blocked (exit 2), with stop_hook_active true it allowed (exit 0). One block per unit.
Covered by TestRunDriver_ACapStopConcludesNothing. Consistent with what I observed: every non-converged stop I produced left the cycle exactly where the completed units put it.

The comparison is against the value §7 actually resolves: I raised run_max_units through the project config to 100, then TP_UNATTENDED=1 tp set run_max_units=101 was refused and =100/=50 accepted. The refusal tracks the resolved value, not a hardcoded default.
Ran it: SIGINT 1.5s into an iteration of 4-second children gave stop_reason interrupted, exit 4, all three children recorded exit 0 with wall_clock 4s (they finished), and no further unit spawned.

Ran it on three different non-converged stops. The log shows 'args=one two' (split on whitespace, no shell), TP_STOP_REASON escalation/unit-failure/interrupted, TP_RUN_ID, and TP_ESCALATION_PATH only on the escalation. The notify script exits 7; the run's stop_reason was unchanged and the exit code was reported in the run surface.

All three registrations in hooks.json declare timeout 10, and the fourth script (pre-tool-use-role-write-allow.sh) is registered by agents/tp-reviewer.md:9 and tp-auditor.md:9 with timeout 10 as well. Every hook I ran exited non-zero on refusal rather than hanging.

agentByKind maps exactly implement->tp-implementer, review-role->tp-reviewer, audit-role->tp-auditor, and BuiltinRunner appends --agent only for a kind in that map, before the budget pair. The other five kinds are absent from the map, so they get no flag.

Ran both halves. Oracle: after three roles wrote valid files, the next iteration and a whole second run omitted all three. Driver: clearUnitArtifacts deletes the findings file and any .part of every role unit the oracle did return, immediately before spawning it.

The experiment that could have failed: in an implement-phase run (round null) I set runner.env TP_ROUND_DIR=/forged and dumped the child env - TP_ROUND_DIR was absent entirely, not empty and not /forged. ChildEnv deletes both round variables whatever the parent or runner.env carried.

readEscalation is consulted independently of the exit code, and the record's path is derived from this attempt's own seq so a previous attempt's record cannot be read as this one's. Live, children exiting 2 with a valid record stopped the run as escalation with no attempt charged.

Mutation-style check through the Stop hook, which applies the same predicate: a .part holding {"a":1} was allowed and the same file rewritten to 'nope' was blocked with 'has a line that is not a JSON object'.

Ran four inputs: zero-byte -> exit 0, blank/whitespace-only -> exit 0, a file whose sole content line is malformed -> exit 1, and a file mixing one good and one bad line -> exit 0. Blank lines never contribute to the condition.

Ran it: the three review-role rows in run-spec.json carry near-identical durations (0.1818/0.1817/0.1822) meaning they overlapped, while the review-record row that followed ran on its own. TestRunDriver_RoleUnitsRunConcurrently asserts from the seam's timestamps.

Ran the hook with tp absent from PATH (exit 2, install command shown) and with a stub reporting v0.34.0 (exit 2, 'older than the tp plugin's minimum 0.35.0'). A stub reporting v0.35.0 passed and injected orientation.

Ran the exit-0-with-nothing-written case directly: a fake exiting 0 without writing its findings file was retried and ultimately stopped the run unit-failure. Succeeded() requires exitCode==0 AND DurableWrite, so the reverse case falls out of the same conjunction.

All three consumers reach roleFindingsParse/readNDJSONRows semantics. Cross-checked live: a malformed role file was blocked by the Stop hook and re-run by the oracle in a second run, while a valid one was allowed and omitted.

Ran it: --resolve accepts both a 0-based index and a role:item_id selector, writes the same resolved{status,evidence,resolved_at} object as review, and --resolve-all disposed the remaining row and skipped the already-resolved one. --force exists for re-resolving.

Observed exit 4 on unit-failure, cap-units, escalation, interrupted and driver-error; exit 2 on the three usage errors before the loop; exit 0 on --dry-run and --status. TestRunExitCodes_ConvergedExitsZero pins the converged case.

Both role agents register the PreToolUse allowlist over all four write tools with timeout 10, permitting only $TP_ROUND_DIR/role-$TP_UNIT_ID.ndjson.part and the run's escalation record. tp-implementer deliberately registers none, with the reason stated in the definition.

Ran a per-kind map {review-role: ..., default: ...}: the audit-role units dispatched to the default entry and inherited its env. A map without default and an object without cmd each exit 2 with the three-shapes hint.

The record kinds' brief command guards the merge on `[ -f $TP_ROUND_DIR/merged.ndjson ] ||`, so a retried or resumed record unit records the existing merged file rather than replacing the resolved objects review-resolve/audit-fix wrote into it.
Ran it: --dry-run exited 0 with no .tp/run-spec.json and no run lock file; --status exited 0 when it could report and 3 with a hint when no run state existed.

Verified through the Stop hook, which applies the same rule: a .part of only blank lines was allowed, and a trailing newline never failed a role. readNDJSONRows trims and skips empty lines before parsing.

Ran two consecutive tp run invocations over the same cycle: run 1 completed the three roles and failed the record unit; run 2 skipped the roles entirely and resumed at review-record (totals.units 2). Nothing was lost or repeated.

Ran both cases. The seam template passes {log_path}, so the driver opened no file and the child's stdout went nowhere - and spend read null because nothing was in the log. A fake writing to the handed path produced the spend the driver read. childOwnsLog gates the redirect.

Ran both halves with a gate of `sh -c "echo GATE-OUTPUT-MARKER; exit 3"`. With TP_UNIT_KIND set, last_failure was written with exit_code 3 and summary 'gate: ...; output: GATE-OUTPUT-MARKER'. With the variable absent, tp done still exited 4 and no last_failure file appeared.
Ran a fake whose body includes `cat` on stdin: it returned immediately with an empty read rather than hanging, and the whole iteration finished in 0.18s. cmd.Stdin = nil gives /dev/null.

Caps are evaluated between iterations only, so nothing is killed mid-flight. Observed the same shape under SIGINT: all three 4-second children ran to completion. TestRunDriver_ACapTrippingMidIterationKillsNothing pins the cap case.
Ran five values plus unset against the same raise: '1' -> 2, 'true' -> 2, 'yes' -> 2, '0' -> 0, '' -> 0, unset -> 0. Present, non-empty and not 0, exactly as documented.

A per-kind map with one unmetered kind: 'spend is not metered for review-role: their runner declares no spend_key, so run_max_budget_usd accrues only the other kinds'. Once each, at run start.

concurrentBatch fans out role units and truncates to one for any non-concurrent kind. Observed live: three review-role children ran together, then the review-record unit ran alone.

taskIsDone reads status==done from disk; UnitImplement is non-concurrent. Live: the implement unit ran alone and a gate failure left it not-done, so the attempt failed.

roleFindingsParse requires the file to exist and every content line to parse. Verified by mutation: a valid one-line file passed, an unparseable line failed, blank-only passed. Roles run concurrently (observed three at once).

allRowsDisposed requires every merged row to carry the resolved object; an absent or unparseable merged file fails. Confirmed the disposition shape against tp audit --resolve output I generated live.
taskFileHasTasks: the init shell holds zero tasks, so an import that wrote nothing is not a completed decompose. Verified against a freshly inited project whose task file had no tasks.
Same predicate as review-role, same parallel concurrency. Observed three audit-role children spawned together in the audit phase of my scratch project.
merged.ndjson plus an audit round file for the round, solo. Mirrors the review-record branch byte for byte in structure.
